welcome.autosave:
There's now a folder named Twine in your Documents folder. Inside that is a Stories folder, where all your work will be saved. Twine saves as you work, so you don't have to worry about remembering to save it yourself. You can always open the folder your stories are saved to by using the Show Library item in the Twine menu.

Because Twine is always saving your work, the files in your story library will be locked from editing while Twine is open.

If you'd like to open a Twine story file you received from someone else, you can import it into your library using the Import From File link in the story list.
welcome.browserStorage:
That means you don't need to create an account to use Twine 2, and everything you create isn't stored on a server somewhere else—it stays right in your browser.

Two very important things to remember, though. Since your work is saved only in your browser, if you clear its saved data, then you'll lose your work! Not good. Remember to use that Archive button often. You can also publish individual stories to files using the menu on each story in the story list. Both archive and story files can always be re-imported into Twine.

Secondly, anyone who can use this browser can see and make changes to your work. So if you've got a nosy kid brother, look into setting up a separate profile for yourself.
welcome.browserStorageTitle: Your work is only saved in your browser
welcome.done: Thanks for reading, and have fun with Twine.

welcome.help: If you've never used Twine before, then welcome! The Twine Cookbook is a great resource for learning how to use it. If you haven't used Twine before, it's a great place to start.

events.delay: Seconds after the condition became true
events.delayHint: 0 — at once. The countdown runs in the background and survives screen changes and crashes; if the condition turns false meanwhile, it is cancelled.
events.priorityHint: If several events are ready at once, the higher number goes first (default 0). The next one waits until players leave the event screen.
events.hint: The terminal goes to this screen by itself when the condition becomes true. An open message window closes. To bring players back, add a link with the action “Return to the previous screen”. In the text: first line <<sg-event …>> and tag sg-event.
events.confirmRemove: The screen stops being an event (the first line <<sg-event …>> and the tag are removed, the rest of the text stays). Remove?
events.noTag: The passage has no sg-event tag — the terminal will not go to it.

ticker.title: Event line

intro.news: Messages of the top line on the main screen. Conditions and limits are checked all the time on any screen; the line is shown on the main screen only.
intro.line: The line sits on one screen only. Its frame matches the terminal window. On-screen buttons from the top corners move down by the line height.
intro.cycle: “Цикл XXXXX” in the top right corner. Its value depends on the progress variable.

ticker.demoHint: Main screen preview: settings apply at once, no sound.

news.name: Name
news.nameHint: For you only, players do not see it. Each message has its own name.
news.textHint: You can insert a variable: <<= $name>>. Text that fits stays still, longer text scrolls.
news.generalHint: Only one general message is shown: the one switched on last. Otherwise it takes turns with the others.
news.minutesHint: 0 — no limit. Counted on any screen.
news.priorityHint: Within the queue: higher goes first. Equal — by list order.

line.screenHint: The screen that shows the line. By default — the story's start screen.
line.speedHint: For text that does not fit in the line.
line.pauseHint: How long the text stays before it moves.
line.holdHint: For text that fits. Long text changes once it has scrolled.
line.orderHint: Message queue. Within each group — by priority, then list order.

cycle.variableHint: When the variable changes, the cycle changes.
cycle.rowsHint: The row with the highest progress not above the current one is used. None — 00000.
cycle.spinTitle: Digit change on the main screen
cycle.spinHint: Only changed digits and those to the right of them spin. The rightmost stops first.
cycle.soundHint: Plays when players see the counter: on entering the main screen, or at once if they are already there.
cycle.gapHint: Time until the next digit to the left stops. 0 means all at once.
cycle.ratesHint: Changes per second. Speed moves smoothly from start to end and cuts off when the digit stops. Gradual slowdown: 20 and 2. Almost no slowdown and a sharp stop: 30 and 20.
cycle.fontHint: Default is DSEG7, as on the timer display.

screens.none: No screen views yet: create them in Terminal Appearance
screens.intro: A preset for special screens: lockdown, alarm, loading. Assign it with the Screen view button above the text. Anything not set comes from the General tab. The preview on the right shows the chosen view on the chosen screen; nothing is written to the story.
screens.name: Name
screens.nameHint: You can rename it: screens keep the view.

list.confirmDeleteUsed: Screen view “{{name}}” is used by {{count}} screen(s). They will become regular. Delete?

screens.sizeHint: On-screen buttons and pictures stay where they are on regular screens.
screens.winBgHint: For a full fill: full-screen window and a custom window background.
screens.textColorHint: Link and button colors come from their kind.

textStyles.none: No text styles yet: create them in Terminal Appearance
textStyles.intro: A preset for individual text: select it in the passage and pick a style with the Text style button. Anything not set stays as the surrounding text. The preview shows a sample; it is not written to the story.
textStyles.name: Name
textStyles.lineHeightHint: Text with its own spacing becomes a separate block: good for a paragraph, not a word within a line.

list.confirmDeleteUsed: Style “{{name}}” is used on {{count}} screen(s). The text stays, without the style. Delete?

access.title: Screen access
access.sharedHint: One for the whole game, for screens without their own. It is an ordinary passage and gets the sg-lock tag.
access.noLock: No lock passage is chosen. Until one is, a link with this behavior cannot be clicked and a code answers “Wrong code”.
access.sourcesHint: What each source does while the screen is closed. The top row of a group is the default; below it each source can have its own behavior.
access.hint: The condition is checked all the time: a link appears as soon as the screen opens. A code is checked before its actions, so an early code is not used up. The preview shows all links; check with Play. In the text: the first line <<sg-access …>> and the sg-access tag.
access.confirmRemove: The screen becomes open to everyone (the <<sg-access …>> command and the tag are removed, the rest of the text stays). Remove?
access.noTag: The passage has no sg-access tag: the terminal lets everyone through.

articles.title: Article
articles.name: Title in the list
articles.sectionHint: No commas. The section joins the choice list once the text is saved.
articles.orderHint: Lower number goes higher; ties go by title. Sections follow their topmost article.
articles.backHint: Empty: the shared caption from Terminal appearance → Articles.
articles.hint: The article appears in “Article list” blocks by itself. The terminal adds a “Back” link at the bottom, leading to the screen the article was opened from. To close an article use “Access”, like any screen.
articles.noTag: This passage has no sg-article tag, so lists will not show it.
articles.confirmRemove: The passage stops being an article and leaves the lists. The text stays. Remove?

first.none: No ways yet — create them in “Terminal appearance”
first.intro: How the elements of a screen appear when players enter it for the first time. A way is set only on the screens you choose: use the “First visit” button above the screen text. Later visits and a restore after a crash open the screen as usual. The “Show” button above the preview plays the selected way on the selected screen.
first.name: Name
first.timeHint: Noise or interference fades to zero over this time.
first.stepHint: Elements go from top to bottom; a line of text is one element. 0 — all together.
first.color: Colour of noise and interference lines
first.skip: A click shows everything at once
first.skipHint: Links and buttons that have not appeared yet cannot be clicked.
first.howTo: Glitch colours are the ones in “Text effects” on the “General” tab. The alarm screen is not affected.

list.confirmDeleteUsed: Way “{{name}}” is used on {{count}} screen(s). They will open as usual. Delete?

first.soundHint: Plays once per screen, from the first element to the end of the file. A click or leaving the screen does not cut it off.

tips.title: Hover tooltip
tips.contentHint: The cursor rests on it. It can hold a link.
tips.widthHint: 0 means as in Terminal appearance. Short text takes only the room it needs.

check.title: Story check
check.intro: Things that will show up as errors in the live game. The story is not changed; click a passage name to open it.
check.noFolder: No game folder chosen — files were not checked.

kinds.media: File missing from the game folder

hints.screen: A link, button, dialog, insert or command leads to a passage that does not exist.
hints.media: The path is written in the story, but the file is not in the game folder.
hints.variable: The variable is used but has no starting value in the Variables window. Not always an error.
hints.code: The code has no actions, no answer and no destination.

copies.title: Radio tracks without a reversed copy
copies.hint: The story has a radio with reverse: these tracks can't play backwards yet (the game shows “REVERSE UNAVAILABLE”). Copies are also made when you press Save in the Music and Radio windows.

music.title: Music
music.intro: The shared player catalogue: Atmosphere and Radio sections with folders and tracks. One track plays at a time; one volume (00–99).
music.spinHint: Digits spin and stop right to left. 0 — at once.
music.autoHint: When a track ends, the next one of the folder plays.
music.tracksHint: Track order is the AUTO order.
music.when: When the track is in the catalogue
music.startHint: On first play the shared volume becomes this.

problems.emptyTrack: A track has no name or file.
problems.slash: A track name contains “/”: that is how “Folder/Track” is written.
problems.noTarget: A transmission leads to a radio folder that does not exist.

music.tipHint: Shown on hover in the Atmosphere catalog.
music.airHint: Transmissions for the repaired radio: each time the screen opens they take random places on the dial. A caught transmission appears in its radio folder.
music.confirmDeleteNested: Delete folder “{{name}}” with its subfolders ({{nested}}) and all tracks?
music.gainHint: 100% — as recorded. Make a loud file quieter to match others; the overall 00–99 volume applies on top.
music.toHint: The caught transmission appears in this radio folder.
music.toNone: Nowhere: interference, never in the catalog
music.widthHint: How many MHz on each side of the transmission it is heard. Closer needle — louder.
music.textHint: Shown in the radio ticker until caught. Empty — the radio view message.
music.whenAir: When the transmission is on air
music.reverseHint: What is heard while REVERSE is held. Empty — the program reverses the track on Save.
music.jamHint: Interference of radios with the air: one folder per radio view from the Radio window, in its order (folders are not created by hand). Each time the radio screen opens, “from”…“to” pieces land on the dial: one already caught piece of this radio, the rest not yet caught ones of this radio and the radios above it; if short — more caught ones of this radio. Interference can be caught like a transmission: it goes to the radio catalog, folder “Interference”.
music.jamMigrated: Interference of radio “{{names}}” moved here from the Radio window. Press Save.
music.jamFolderHint: Named after the radio view: rename the view in the Radio window, the folder follows.
music.jamOrphan: There is no radio view with this name. This interference is not used — the folder can be deleted.
music.whenJam: When this interference can land on the dial
music.jamWidthHint: How many MHz on each side of its spot it can be heard.

screenMusic.title: Screen music
screenMusic.intro: Change music some seconds after entering.
screenMusic.afterHint: From the start of the fade.

radio.title: Radio
radio.name: Look name
radio.nameHint: Radio blocks find the look by name.
radio.typeHint: Repaired — with the air; with reverse — plus REVERSE and reels; with decoder — as with reverse plus DECODE and a picture window. Progress bar and SHUFFLE — on all.
radio.elementsHint: Everything without its own colour below.
radio.label: Frame label
radio.confirmDeleteUsed: Look “{{name}}” is used on {{count}} screens. Delete?

problems.slash: A view name can't contain “/” (it names the interference folder in the Music window).

radio.airHint: Scale 88–108 MHz, drag the needle, −/+ move 0.1 at most once a second. Landing on a broadcast with the buttons lights the lamp. SEARCH pauses catalogue music. Broadcasts are in the Music window, Air section.
radio.incomingHint: The ticker shows it while an uncaught transmission is on air. A transmission may have its own.
radio.catchHint: Seconds the needle must stay exactly on a transmission to catch it.
radio.noiseHint: Plays in its ranges, quieter near transmissions and interference, silent on exact tuning.
radio.jamsHint: Each time the screen opens a random set is chosen and placed randomly on the dial; nearby ones play together.
radio.jamWidthHint: How many MHz on each side it is heard.
radio.jamsMaxHint: In this radio's folder: {{files}}; not yet caught interference of the radios above also lands. Each piece — once.
radio.asFrame: Now the same as the frame: partitions, grille, reels.
radio.reverseHint: While REVERSE is held the track plays backwards. The program makes reversed copies on Save (here and in Music), into media/audio/reverse.
radio.decoderHint: DECODE turns the decoder on: if the playing track or the loudest spot of the air carries an SSTV picture, it builds line by line in time with the sound; off-tune — noisy lines, not SSTV — garbage lines. Click the window — full terminal, click again — back. Pictures are taken from interference and transmissions when you press Save in the Music window.
radio.jamsMoved: Interference of this radio is in the Music window, section Interference, folder “{{name}}” (now: {{count}}). Here — how many land at once.
radio.orderHint: The order of views is the order of radios in the game: interference of the radios above also lands on the radios below.

reverse.noFolder: No game folder — reversed copies not made.

sstv.working: Looking for SSTV pictures in interference and transmissions: {{done}} of {{total}}…
sstv.noFolder: No game folder — SSTV pictures were not searched.
